done_when: brief.md lets a worker update tests when the Done-when deliberately changes behaviour, explaining the old and new contract, and never weaken a test to hide a defect; brief.md says a failure is unrelated only with a matching failure on the default branch, else unresolved; review.md and standards.md say doc-only changes need no new behaviour test, only checked claims, commands and links; standards.md and brief.md say joining lines or removing blank lines never counts as a reduction; skill.md says to read the worker's final handoff and resolve stated blockers before forge close; the generated skill copies match; a test through the real commands shows each sentence reaches its reader
why: Workers stop, reviews chase and handoffs mislead for reasons one sentence of instruction would prevent: tests that must change with an intended behaviour change, test demands on doc-only changes, failures called unrelated without evidence, line cuts by reformatting, and closes started on a worker's unfinished handoff
